name: Western Digital Corporation

sections.title: Quarterly revenue
sections.callout: Outlook: Western Digital guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to about $4.1B, plus or minus $100M, with a 55%–56% non-GAAP gross margin.

footnotes: Sandisk stake gain & other is interest and other income, net, which includes a $6.5B gain on Western Digital's retained Sandisk shares. FY2025 net income includes $246M from discontinued operations (the flash business spun off as Sandisk).
Fiscal 2026 was a 53-week year ended Jul 3, 2026. Full-year revenue by end market was not in the release, so the flow chart shows revenue by quarter. Free cash flow as reported.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Western Digital, now a pure hard-drive company after spinning off Sandisk, grew revenue 35.7% to $12.9B in fiscal 2026 on cloud and AI storage demand. Gross margin rose to 48.9% and operating income nearly doubled to $4.5B.
Net income was $9.4B, boosted by a $6.5B gain on its remaining Sandisk shares. Free cash flow reached $3.5B, debt fell 77.7% to $1.1B, and the company bought back $2.6B of stock.
highlights: Q4 FY2026 revenue reached a record $3.7B, up 43.8%.
Free cash flow rose 2.5 times to $3.5B.
watch: Most of net income came from a one-time $6.5B gain on Sandisk shares.
Cash fell 25.3% to $1.6B after debt repayment and buybacks.
Results depend heavily on cloud data-center spending.
sources: Western Digital fiscal Q4 and FY2026 results (SEC 8-K)
